1.?

limx→5x−1−2x−5=

M
Sat, Aug 22nd @ 2:07 PM|Elapsed: 5:48Correct

If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form: limx→5x−1−2x−5=5−1−25−5=00

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

limx→5x−1−2x−5=limx→5(x−1−2)(x−1+2)(x−5)(x−1+2)=limx→5(x−1)2−22(x−5)(x−1+2)=limx→5x−1−4(x−5)(x−1+2)=limx→5x−5(x−5)(x−1+2)=limx→51x−1+2=15−1+2=14.
